dedupe_keys.name: epa smart location database and national walkability index us census block groups

description: EPA's Smart Location Mapping products measure the built environment and transit accessibility of every US census block group, to support travel demand, land use and transport planning. The Smart Location Database holds more than 90 indicators of density (housing, population and jobs per acre of unprotected land), diversity of land use (jobs per housing unit, employment and housing entropy), urban design (intersection and high-speed road density), transit service frequency, destination accessibility, employment and demographics; a beta came out in 2011, the first full version in 2013 and version 3 in 2021. The National Walkability Index ranks each block group against all others by a weighted formula of four ranked inputs: employment and housing mix, employment mix, pedestrian-oriented intersection density and predicted carpool share, each ranked 1 to 20. Coverage: all US block groups for most attributes; transit indicators only where agencies share service data. Access: ZIP downloads, interactive map viewers and ArcGIS web services, with a user guide and methodology. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): Public domain (EPA web policy: EPA-produced data are in the public domain unless otherwise specified). Access is free of charge. Caveats: the index is relative to the national set, and users must recompute it to rank within a state or city. Simulation uses are neighbourhood form and walkability inputs for travel behaviour, activity and public space models. Related records: Can-ALE, the comparable Canadian index.
